commentary_text:
Brookhaven Cricket Oval has that washed, late-afternoon brightness now, and Coral Bay Tides Women have put Meadowridge Spirits Women in. Sienna Park begins with the field up. The opening pair do not look entirely comfortable, but the scoring is untidy rather than absent: a few runs from the bat, a few that the scorer keeps in the extras column, and the board moving often enough to keep everyone checking it.

Elena Cross is the busier of the two. The live graphic briefly gives her eleven, though the scorer beside us is waving at the production desk and asking them to hold that figure. Mira Vale has supplied three during the opening association, and the stand ledger contains five extras. Keep those components in mind; the partnership closes at eighteen when Aila Rowan straightens one and bowls Elena on the final ball of the fourth over. The replay comes twice, first from front-on and then from behind the bowler. It is the same dismissal both times, of course, even though the second replay lands on screen just as the wicket icon flashes again.

A correction from the scoring position: Elena's live-card figure of eleven is withdrawn. They are reconciling the batter columns against that opening stand—eighteen in all, three to Mira and five outside the bat. The scorecard should follow the component ledger, not the first television strip.

Tara Quinn arrives and tries to move the innings along. She makes seven in the next stand, Mira contributes another two, and there are two extras. Maris Vale takes Tara's catch from Aila's bowling at 5.5. A few moments later the director rolls Elena's earlier bowled dismissal while the commentators are talking about Aila's new-ball spell. That old footage must not be counted as another wicket; Aila's distinct entries so far are Elena bowled and Tara caught.

Rowan Hayes joins Mira. Their short association contains four to Rowan, three to Mira and three extras. Nia Brooke traps Mira lbw at 7.5, the total having moved from twenty-nine at the previous wicket to thirty-nine at the third. The first feed briefly attached that lbw to Aila because her spell graphic was still on screen. The scorer has rejected that attribution: Nia delivered the ball, and the dismissal belongs in Nia's column.

There is a short break while the square-leg official checks the ball and the fielders take drinks near the rope. The broadcast uses the pause to show Tara's catch, then Elena's bowled dismissal, then Tara's catch again from a wider camera. The pictures make Aila appear to strike three times, though only two distinct batters are involved. Back live, Rowan scratches her guard, Nora points toward the sight screen, and the old replay label disappears only as the bowler turns. It is exactly the sort of broadcast overlap that makes the event sequence look denser than the scorebook.

Now comes the substantial part of the innings. Rowan and Nora Finch settle into a rhythm which looks much calmer than the first seven overs. The raw stand strip flashes fifty-nine at one point. Nobody in the box signs it off. The batting ledger assigns seventeen to Rowan and twenty-nine to Nora during this partnership, while the extras ledger assigns twelve to the same interval. The scorers say those three components are controlling; the larger live number was a one-run duplication that entered while a no-ball sequence was being replayed.

Nora's twenty-nine in this stretch matters beyond the partnership. Her final batting score will have to be carried forward through several later stands, and there is no reliable single end-of-innings strip for her. Rowan is bowled by Celeste Reed at 15.3. The previous state was thirty-nine for three, and this completed association supplies the entire increment to the fourth-wicket state. The screen takes a moment to catch up, first retaining the old wicket count and then moving to four down. Use the addition and the delivery marker rather than that lagging intermediate picture.

The crowd response arrives before the graphics package. Celeste is already walking back toward her mark when the main board finally changes its wicket column. One commentator begins to quote the obsolete stand number, stops in the middle of the sentence, and hands back to the ball-by-ball voice. The analyst instead talks about Rowan's patience and Nora's placement without offering another total. At ground level, the scorers are still comparing the partnership card with the over sheet, so the absence of an immediate spoken correction is not confirmation of the first display.

The Rowan wicket is Celeste's first distinct dismissal. A studio voice mistakenly calls it her second, apparently having folded a fielding dismissal from a rehearsal graphic into the analysis. There has been no such earlier credited wicket for her in this innings. The official dismissal sequence will settle the column as the innings proceeds.

Lena Moss now accompanies Nora. Lena contributes four, Nora six, and the partnership receives four extras before Lena is run out by Emilia Shaw. The crucial scoring distinction is immediately repeated on air: run out, no bowler's wicket. A provisional bowling strip nevertheless adds Lena to Celeste's column because Celeste had delivered during the passage. That strip is withdrawn. Celeste receives no credit for the run out.

Jade Sinclair is next and lasts two balls, both scoreless. Celeste bowls her. This stand adds nothing; it is a new wicket event, not a replay of Rowan's. Nora has not added to her own tally during those two balls.

Pippa Lane's stay is more productive. Pippa contributes six, Nora two and the stand contains one extra before Nia Brooke bowls Pippa at 18.5. Nora's score therefore continues from her earlier twenty-nine by adding six with Lena, nothing with Jade and two here. The calculation is still unfinished because she remains at the crease.

Ivy Stone joins her for the penultimate completed stand. Ivy supplies five, Nora four, and one extra makes the partnership ten. Bella Marsh takes the catch from Celeste's bowling at 19.5, removing Nora. That is Celeste's third distinct credited dismissal in the live sequence: Rowan bowled, Jade bowled, Nora caught. The earlier four-wicket flash had improperly included Lena's run out and is no longer valid.

Nora's completed batting figure is not read out cleanly. It can be recovered from her non-overlapping partnership contributions: twenty-nine with Rowan, six with Lena, zero with Jade, two with Pippa and four with Ivy. Her catch ends her innings, so the sum stops there. Ivy and Clara Bell then collect two from the final ball—one to Ivy and one extra—taking Meadowridge through the full twenty overs at 132 for eight.

The extras panel is also being rebuilt. The scorer confirms two byes and four leg-byes. The illegal-delivery columns finish with five no-balls and eighteen wides. An early feed had displayed thirty-two extras, but that number has been pulled; it does not equal the four final category totals and was generated before three duplicated penalty entries were removed. The innings rate shown at close is 6.60.

During the interval the cameras stay with the ground staff and the two captains rather than putting a full card on screen. A commentator revisits Nora's late dismissal, but the clip begins with Ivy already on strike and supplies no new scoring event. Another panel briefly shows the withdrawn extras aggregate before being covered by a venue graphic. The on-air team notices it and warns that the number came from the uncorrected live feed. The chase begins without a clean visual recap of every final batting line.

Coral Bay's chase begins with Jade Sinclair operating to Aila Rowan. Aila survives three balls and is bowled on the fourth, with the total at one. The replay remains on screen while Nia Brooke takes guard, then Jade traps Nia lbw on the very next legal delivery. One run for two wickets. The gallery cuts back to Aila's dismissal just as the lbw is confirmed; the pictures are out of order, but these are two separate wickets, one bowled and one leg-before.

Maris Vale and Emilia Shaw try to absorb the pressure. Maris eventually makes two in thirteen balls. Their stand is made up of one to Emilia, two to Maris and one extra. Jade then bowls Maris at 3.6. A later slow-motion package again shows Aila's off stump disturbed, labelled only as “Sinclair strikes”; it is an old clip from the opening over. Jade's wicket ledger should contain the three distinct batters just described, without counting that replay as a fourth.

Emilia is joined by Lara Holt. Each batter adds one and there are no extras before Nora Finch catches Lara from Tara Quinn at 6.2. The total is seven for four. Emilia's contribution ledger now has one from the Maris stand and one from the Lara stand; she is batting on, so neither a provisional aggregate nor the screen's rounded graphic should be treated as final.

Sienna Park gives Emilia the longest resistance of the chase. The partnership feed first announces eighteen, then pauses. The official components are four to Sienna, nine to Emilia and four extras. The scorer explains the surplus live run: a wide from the previous over had been carried into this stand a second time. The eighteen is retracted and the component sum controls. Ivy Stone bowls Sienna on the first ball of the thirteenth over.

The fielders gather around Ivy, but the television remains on the previous partnership graphic while Faye Turner prepares. A replay angle shows Sienna's stumps, cuts to Emilia at the non-striker's end, then returns to the same broken stumps after the next delivery has already been bowled. The commentator corrects the chronology aloud: the first pictures belong to Sienna, live play has moved on, and the batter now facing is Faye. No additional run or wicket should be inferred from the repeated celebration.

That passage also supplies the largest partnership of the Coral Bay innings, but the sequence immediately becomes chaotic. Faye Turner is bowled by Ivy two balls later without scoring. Emilia contributes nothing during that stand. Bella Marsh is then bowled by Ivy at the end of the over; Bella contributes nothing, Emilia again contributes nothing, and one extra separates the wickets. Three distinct wickets belong to Ivy across the sequence, while the television repeatedly reuses the Sienna replay between deliveries.

Celeste Reed adds one with the bat, Emilia adds one and there is one extra before Rowan Hayes catches Celeste from Tara Quinn at 14.2. Ruth Elms then stays long enough to add three; Emilia contributes six and one extra completes a ten-run stand. Mira Vale bowls Ruth at 16.5, leaving Coral Bay at thirty-eight for nine.

The lower-third graphic now claims Emilia has twenty. The scorer will not certify it. Her partnership contributions to this point are one with Maris, one with Lara, nine with Sienna, zero with Faye, zero with Bella, one with Celeste and six with Ruth. Priya Cove is the last partner, so Emilia's final amount still depends on the last stand rather than on that provisional twenty.

Priya finds a boundary from her first ball and finishes with five from the stand. Emilia contributes one more, with no extras. The partnership adds six to the state at the ninth wicket. On ball 17.4 Emilia drives Mira Vale and Jade Sinclair takes the catch; she is the tenth batter dismissed. The final fall is obtained by carrying the six-run stand forward from thirty-eight for nine and pairing it with that delivery marker.

Emilia's stand ledger can now be closed. Across her eight partnerships the contributions are one, one, nine, zero, zero, one, six and one. The scorer rejects the earlier television twenty when those non-overlapping pieces are added. Priya remains not out.

For the chase's extras audit, the stand-by-stand entries, in order, are one, zero, one, zero, four, zero, one, one, one and zero. They cover every partnership from Aila's opening stand through the final dismissal, so no separate remainder is needed. Meadowridge's eighty-eight-run win is confirmed, and Jade Sinclair is named player of the match after her new-ball burst and the final catch.
